title: MSA & Order Form — public disclosure / logo use redlines
text:
MSA & Order Form — public disclosure / logo use redlines

["From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Houston <jane.houston@acme.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA & Order Form — press & logos (initial redlines)

Jane —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our call, attaching a first-pass redline of our standard MSA + Order Form with the publicity / logo-use and reference rights highlighted. A few quick clarifications we want on your side before legal redlines are finalized: 

- Is ACME asking for a perpetual right to use Redwood's name/logo in customer lists or only a time-limited case study/press mention?
- For press releases, do you require a 10-business-day embargo (we typically ask for 3–5 days for coordination)?
- Are you seeking any anonymity or redaction (e.g., remove product names) for the quoted language?

Attachments: redwood-redlines-msav.docx (redline: MSA + OF, publicity sections annotated)

My proposed approach: we can accept a limited reference right for case studies and press with a short embargo and approval step — but we should keep an explicit carveout that allows Redwood to publish general product descriptions without customer-specific confidential data.

Can you have your legal send back a marked-up PDF? If you want us to put the changes into tracked language we can do that as well.

Next steps: if you confirm the embargo window and whether ACME wants logo assets to be stored in a shared library, I’ll loop in Markus (legal/negotiation) for final language.

Best,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

---
Attachment: redwood-redlines-msav.docx", "From: Jane Houston <jane.houston@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, ACME Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — press & logos (initial redlines)

Ben —

Thanks for sending the redline. Attached are ACME's comments (ACME_redlines.pdf). High level:

- We are looking for the ability to include Redwood in a public customer list indefinitely unless you object to a specific use — that is our preferred commercial model for platform vendors.
- For press releases mentioning ACME specifically, we request a 7-business-day review period.
- We would like the ability to quote a short, approved testimonial and use the Redwood logo on our marketing site and partner collateral.

We flagged a few specific clauses where ACME's legal wants: (a) narrower carveouts around competitive use; (b) confirmation that Redwood will not identify any ACME customers or project-level metrics without explicit permission; (c) a short exceptions process for pre-approved joint announcements.

I copied our legal team. They can take point on negotiating the exact language, but wanted to understand Redwood's comfort with the indefinite customer-list permission.

On the embargo: 7 business days is what our comms team prefers; would Redwood accept 5 as a compromise?

Thanks,

Jane Houston
Head of Strategic Ops — Acme Corp
jane.houston@acme.com

On Thu, May 28, 2026 at 9:12 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jane —
> 
> Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our call, attaching a first-pass redline of our standard MSA + Order Form with the publicity / logo-use and reference rights highlighted...

---
Attachment: ACME_redlines.pdf", 'From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MSA & Order Form — press & logos (please review)

Team —

Forwarding ACME's reply and redlines. Two points I want legal to weigh in on and we should propose concrete language back to ACME: 

1) Customer list permission (indefinite vs. time-limited). Ben, commercial asks for indefinite listing; ACME expects that by default — we should protect our right to opt out of specific uses and keep a carveout that prevents use of our trademarked marketing assets in paid ads. Proposed middle-ground: "ACME grants Redwood a non-exclusive, perpetual, revocable-right (subject to ACME's written objection to specific uses) to list ACME as a Redwood customer in materials, provided Redwood does not imply endorsement or use ACME intellectual property beyond logo assets provided for the purpose." 

2) Press release / embargo timing: ACME requests 7 business days. I think 5 business days is acceptable. We should add an approval-limited clause that prevents unreasonable withholding (e.g., must respond within the window or consent is deemed granted).

Kimberly — can you draft suggested language for (a) customer-list/reference rights, (b) logo use (limited to provided assets and specified templates), and (c) a standard approval/embargo clause that includes a deemed-approved fallback if no response within the stated window?

Please include short rationale in-line so I can share with Jane if needed.

-Markus

---
Original message attached: ACME_redlines.pdf', 'From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Jane Houston <jane.houston@acme.com>
Cc: ACME Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — press & logos (suggested compromise language)

Jane / Ben / Markus —

Thanks for the clear notes. I've drafted compromise language below and attached a plain-text snippet (PR_clause_suggested_text.txt) you can drop into the MSA. High-level approach: preserve ACME's commercial ask for broad reference rights while protecting Redwood's brand controls and preventing implied endorsement.

1) Customer list / reference rights (suggested language):
"Customer may include Redwood in public lists of vendors and partners indefinitely. Redwood may list Customer as a Redwood customer only if (a) Customer has not delivered a written objection to the specific use within 10 business days of receipt of notice; and (b) Redwood's listing does not use Customer's trademarks beyond logo assets expressly provided by Customer for public use, nor imply endorsement of Redwood's products beyond a short permitted testimonial."

Rationale: gives ACME indefinite listing while creating a short objection window and explicit trademark limitations to protect both sides.

2) Logo use and templates:
"Customer will provide approved logo assets and usage guidelines. Redwood's use of Customer logos shall be limited to the supplied asset files and follow Customer's branding guidelines. Redwood will not place Customer logos on paid advertising without prior written consent."

3) Press release / embargo and approval process:
"For joint press releases or releases identifying Customer by name, the parties agree to a 5-business-day review period following delivery of a final draft to the other party. If the recipient does not provide written objections within the review period, consent will be deemed granted. Objections must be reasonable and limited to confidential information or material inaccuracies; in the event of a dispute, parties will escalate to their respective senior marketing or legal contacts."

Action items: 
- Ben: share the attached plain-text clause with Jane and ACME legal for review (Done).
- Markus: if ACME pushes for 7 days, I'm ok to give 7 as a concession but keep the deemed-granted fallback after 10 business days for customer-list objections.
- Jane / ACME Legal: please confirm if this approach addresses your ask for indefinite listing plus testimonial/logo use, or if you need a separate NDA carveout for case-study content.

I attached the PR_clause_suggested_text.txt and a short tracked-change snippet I can incorporate into the Order Form if you want a final redline.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0178

Attachments: PR_clause_suggested_text.txt']
